a01: You just sold a call option. | If the stock rallies, you lose money.
a02: So how does a trading desk sleep at night? | Delta hedging.
a03: Delta tells you how much the option moves | when the stock moves by [one rupee.=₹1.]
a04: Here, delta is about [zero point five,=0.5,] | so for every option you sold, | you buy half a share.
a05: Now if the stock ticks up, | you lose on the option, | but you gain on the shares. | The two almost cancel out.
a06: But delta keeps changing as the stock moves, | so the hedge has to be adjusted, | again and again. That's rebalancing.
a07: Watch one simulated path. | Rebalance [five=5] times, and the hedge drifts.
a08: [Twenty=20] times, it's much closer. | [Two hundred=200] times, the error almost disappears.
a09: The rule of thumb: | rebalance [four=4] times as often, | and the error roughly halves.
a10: But every trade costs money, | so finding that balance | is the real job on the desk.
a11: Try it yourself | in the Stochastic Calculus Visual Lab, | on [Desk to Quant.=Desk2Quant.]
